title: Universal Drag Handles and Drop Zone Highlighting
description: Add a consistent drag-handle affordance (grip-vertical icon) to every draggable UI element in ui/js/react/index.tsx, and highlight all valid drop zones (passively) while a compatible drag is in flight, keeping the existing stronger indicator on the currently hovered target. Handle-only drag initiation on select-first elements (panel tabs, mode/window tabs, reorderable tree rows); whole-surface drag retained on drag-first elements (tree-unit headers, catalogue/palette items, mode tab-gap stack drag, DraggableAvatar). Handles always visible (muted, brighten on hover). Plan approved at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-everything-that-is-silly-wolf.md.
summary:
Fixed a visual-consistency bug in the passive drop-zone highlight from the initial implementation and switched its fill to the secondary accent color per feedback.

Root cause: several tree components (TreeItem, SortableTreeItem, TreeSection) split their row into a "shell" (outer wrapper including the guide gutter, and for TreeItem's property layout, also the nested expanded-content wrapper) and a "content" fill area (label column only, the same area `isSelected`/`isHighlighted` already paint via `treeRowChromeContentFillClasses`/`contentChromeClassName`). The original single combined `dropZoneReadyClass` (dashed outline + low-opacity primary-accent tint) was applied to the shell in these components, so it bled into the gutter and, for expandable property rows, into nested child content — producing a different, inconsistent look per row kind, and also clashed with existing borders (e.g. `PanelEmptyDockZone`'s own dashed border).

Fix: split the constant into `dropZoneReadyFillClass` (`bg-[var(--accent-secondary)]`, the design system's secondary accent — distinct from the primary accent used by the stronger "actively hovered" indicators) and `dropZoneReadyTextClass` (`text-emphasized`, mirrors the existing `treeRowChromeShellClasses`/`interactiveActiveFillClass` selected/active convention so labels and icons read clearly against the fill), plus a combined `dropZoneReadyClass` for single-container consumers that have no shell/content split (panel tabs, panel tree-unit headers, the empty dock zone, mode/window tab bars). Updated TreeItem (all three layouts), SortableTreeItem, and TreeSection to apply the text class to their shell and the fill class to their content-fill class instead of the combined class to the shell, so the fill now paints only the same label-column area as the selected/highlighted states, and dropped the old outline treatment entirely.

Verification: typecheck and lint show the same pre-existing-only results as before (no new errors), `check-no-raw-colors` confirms the new `bg-[var(--accent-secondary)]` arbitrary-value class isn't flagged (it references an existing CSS variable, not a literal color) and index.tsx has zero violations, and the test suite shows the identical 257 passed / 14 pre-existing failures as before this fix. Browser-based visual verification was still not possible — the Browser pane tooling remained unresponsive this session (see prior close note); this should be visually confirmed in a working browser session.
